method: Each page was fetched on the check date and the times were read from the page text. Findings are paraphrased here; the pages themselves are the source. No window is attributed to a particular lecture or year: we found no dated primary source for any of them.

kill_zone_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Killzones

windows.Asian: introduction: roughly 8:00 to 10:00 pm; calculation section: 20:00 to 00:00

what_it_says: Window boundaries differ by 30 to 90 minutes across ICT sources and platforms.
Crypto trades around the clock, yet volatility still tends to cluster near the traditional London and New York opens; test the windows on your instrument before trusting them.
The offset to other time zones drifts during the weeks when the US and UK change clocks on different dates.
No statistics are given. No originator is named beyond 'ICT (Inner Circle Trader) methodology'.

kill_zone_sources.name: LiteFinance: ICT Killzones Explained
kill_zone_sources.time_zone: table gives UTC, BST and EDT columns
what_it_says: The table states that its hours are displayed in daylight saving time.
It advises accounting for the switch between daylight and standard time; it does not give a winter table.
kill_zone_sources.our_reading: We treat these as New York wall-clock times, as the EDT column gives them. Read as fixed UTC hours instead, the London window would be 02:00 to 05:00 New York time in winter, which is LuxAlgo's window. The page does not say which is meant.

kill_zone_sources.name: Equiti: ICT Killzones: London and New York sessions explained
what_it_says: Asian session and London close are mentioned without times.

kill_zone_sources.name: TradingView open-source script: Session Killzones ICT Concept (mahirtrade)
kill_zone_sources.time_zone: New York time, automatic daylight-saving handling

kill_zone_sources.name: TradingView open-source script: ICT Killzones + Macros [TakingProphets]
kill_zone_sources.time_zone: labelled EST; the page does not say whether the times follow daylight saving

kill_zone_sources.name: MQL5 blog: ICT killzones: what they are and how to mark them cleanly (Hacene Harrous)
what_it_says: Gives no clock times and no time zone for either window. Read, not cited in the article.

not_found: A dated primary source (a lecture, a document) in which Michael J. Huddleston fixes the kill zone hours. The article attributes the windows to the pages above, not to him.
Any published measurement of kill-zone activity on crypto perpetuals. LuxAlgo's page asserts clustering near the London and New York opens without figures.

clock_sources.name: NIST: Daylight Saving Time (DST)
what_it_says: US daylight time begins at 2:00 a.m. on the second Sunday of March and ends at 2:00 a.m. on the first Sunday of November; in 2026, 8 March to 1 November.

clock_sources.name: GOV.UK: When do the clocks change?
what_it_says: UK clocks go forward at 1am on the last Sunday in March and back at 2am on the last Sunday in October; in 2026, 29 March and 25 October.

clock_sources.name: NYSE: Holidays and trading hours
what_it_says: Core trading session: 9:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. ET.
